help.title: Help & Features
help.intro: Every Schreibwerkstatt feature by area. “Open” jumps straight there; badges show what a feature needs. With a book open you only see what fits its book type and your role.
help.feat.overview: Each book's home page: size, recently edited sections, chapter distribution, character and location presence, plot and motif status, plus tiles for the latest analyses.
help.feat.review: Reviews the whole book from an editor's perspective: a grade per axis, strengths, weaknesses and concrete improvements with quoted evidence. The axes follow the book type.
help.feat.stil: Style metrics per chapter and section as a heatmap: filler words, passive voice, sentence length, readability, sentence openers and rhythm. Measured from the text, no AI judgement.
help.feat.fehlerHeatmap: Shows where copy-editing findings cluster — by chapter and error type — and how error density develops across drafts.
help.feat.kontinuitaet: Looks for contradictions in the manuscript: conflicting character details, characters in two places at once, broken world rules. Every finding comes with its passages.
help.feat.buchlandkarte: Two tabs over the semantic index. Map: every section as a dot, closeness means related content — reveals chapters telling the same thing or splitting apart, and outliers. Duplicates: scenes told twice and recurring descriptions. Never writes into the text.
help.feat.wortschatz: Length-robust vocabulary metrics (MATTR, MTLD, hapax ratio, lexical density), plus favourite words, recurring phrases and a word cloud.
help.feat.erzaehlprofil: Detects point of view and tense per chapter, flags deviations from the declared narrative mode and shows the tension curve and dominant themes.
help.feat.tagebuchRueckblick: Condenses a period of the diary — month or year — into themes, people, places and notable days.
help.feat.struktur: Sets the text genre per article (news, feature, opinion …) and checks the form against it: lead, structure, counter-position, ending. Language is the copy-editor's job.
help.feat.titelwerkstatt: Kicker, headline, lead and teaser as fields next to the article, with a character counter per channel, AI variants to choose from and the editorial status up to “approved”.
help.feat.figuren: All characters with profile, relationship graph (sociogram) and appearances. The “Age” tab computes ages with evidence, “Life course” puts biographies side by side.
help.feat.werkstatt: Design characters before they appear in the text: a mind map per character, AI brainstorming and a check whether the draft matches the manuscript.
help.feat.szenen: All scenes with chapter, characters, location and rating, filterable. Shows which scenes carry the story and which fall flat.
help.feat.orte: All locations with description, atmosphere, characters involved and chapters — optionally placed on a map.
help.feat.songs: All pieces of music and artists mentioned in the text, with first mention, chapter and the characters who listen to them — the book's taste in music.
help.feat.ereignisse: A global timeline built from all characters' dated events, filterable by character and type. Makes the story's chronology visible.
help.feat.plot: Plan the plot as a beat board: acts as columns, beats as cards, plot lines as lanes. The AI checks the plan against the manuscript; the app re-computes dated beats against birth years and order.
help.feat.motiv: Plan themes and motifs as a constellation and link them to characters, beats, chapters and sections. The AI finds them in the text; a band shows their density.
help.feat.weltfakten: The book's established facts and world rules by category — magic system, technology, geography, society. The basis for the continuity check.
help.feat.recherche: A knowledge board for notes, links, quotes, PDFs and images, linked to characters, locations and scenes. Includes a research chat that searches the web and suggests finds.
help.feat.ideenBoard: All ideas and open items of the book on one board: rows are chapters and sections, columns the status. Discarded items stay as a trace of the decision.
help.feat.sources: Source library: capture sources (also via DOI/ISBN or PDF), assign them to the book and see where they are cited. Citation style selectable, bibliography in every export.
help.feat.bookchat: An agentic chat about the whole book: it queries characters, locations, scenes and full text itself and answers with evidence. Read-only, never changes the text.
help.feat.stats: How the book has grown: characters, words and sections over time, for the whole book and per chapter.
help.feat.bookSettings: Everything about the book: book type, language and narrative mode, context for the AI, publication details, citation style, members and roles, blog sync, merging and deleting.
help.feat.finetuneExport: Generates training data (JSONL) from your texts to fine-tune your own language model on your style.
help.feat.snapshots: Freezes the whole book as a “draft”. Drafts can be compared, opened read-only, exported, marked as a published edition and restored.
help.feat.export: Quick export of a book, chapter or section as HTML, TXT, Markdown, PDF or EPUB — also from a draft. The customisable exports cover designed output.
help.feat.pdfExport: Print-ready PDF with your own typesetting profile: font, page size, cover, front matter, indexes, running heads. Optionally PDF/A for archiving or PDF/X for the printer.
help.feat.epubExport: E-book in EPUB format: choose range, reflow style, cover and table of contents; bibliography included.
help.feat.docxExport: Manuscript as a Word document for editors and publishers: standard manuscript format, front matter, chapter numbering and reusable profiles. Tables become real Word tables.
help.feat.folderImport: Brings text into the app: a Word or ODT manuscript split into chapters and sections at its headings, a diary folder as ZIP, or an export bundle (.swbook).
help.feat.bookOrganizer: Arrange, nest, rename, create and delete chapters, subchapters and sections by drag and drop. Text lives only in sections (any length, not a printed page); chapters provide structure.
help.feat.bookEditor: The whole manuscript as one continuous stream, chapter by chapter. With find & replace across the book and the margin rail for test-reader comments.
help.feat.search: Searches sections, chapters, characters, locations and research — in the open book or across all your books. With a semantic index it also finds passages that say the same in other words.
help.feat.shareLinks: Shares a section, chapter or the whole book via link with test readers — no account needed. Readers comment right in the text; you reply in the reading view or the book editor.
help.feat.onboarding: A guided start in four steps — create a book, write, analyse, share — with real progress tracking and a sample book to try things out.
help.feat.komplett: Reads the whole book in one background run and fills characters, sociogram, locations, scenes, music, world facts, timeline and continuity. Many cards depend on it.
help.feat.myStats: Your writing metrics across all your books: daily goal, writing streaks, size by category and progress over time.
help.feat.myBooks: Every accessible book on one row: size, writing time, drafts, exports, reading links and test-reader comments. Pin, archive, mark as finished.
help.feat.autorenprofil: Places the stylistic metrics of your books side by side in order of writing — sentence structure, vocabulary, readability. Shows how your style evolves.
help.feat.shortcuts: Overview of all keyboard shortcuts, e.g. command palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K), focus editor (⌘⇧E / Ctrl+Shift+E), find, save, undo.
help.extra.editors.title: Three editors
help.extra.editors.desc: Notebook editor for a single section (pick a section, “Edit”), focus editor as a distraction-free full-screen mode (⌘⇧E / Ctrl+Shift+E) and book editor for the whole manuscript. All save automatically.
help.extra.lektorat.title: Copy-editing
help.extra.lektorat.desc: Checks the open section for style breaks, repetitions, weak verbs, passive chains and tense shifts. Every finding jumps to its place and can be applied one by one.
help.extra.pageChat.title: Section chat
help.extra.pageChat.desc: Sparring about the open section, right next to the editor. Suggestions come as text replacements you accept or reject one by one.
help.extra.reference.title: Reference panel
help.extra.reference.desc: A companion panel next to the editor: plan (the chapter's beats from the beat board), characters, locations, scenes, events, research, sources and related passages for the open section or the whole book. For reference only.
help.extra.ideas.title: Section ideas
help.extra.ideas.desc: Capture notes and open items right on a section or chapter, next to the editor. The ideas board later shows them collected for the whole book.
help.extra.spellcheck.title: Spell check
help.extra.spellcheck.desc: Spelling, grammar and style are marked as you type in all three editors, with a one-click correction. Rule-based, no AI.
help.extra.synonyms.title: Synonyms
help.extra.synonyms.desc: Right-click a word in the editor to see synonyms from the thesaurus and, on request, context-aware suggestions from the AI.
help.extra.figurLookup.title: Character lookup
help.extra.figurLookup.desc: ⌘-click or Ctrl-click a character name in the editor to open that character's profile without leaving the text.
help.extra.dictation.title: Dictation
help.extra.dictation.desc: Microphone button in the notebook editor toolbar: speech is inserted verbatim at the cursor at every pause.
help.extra.readAloud.title: Read aloud
help.extra.readAloud.desc: Has the section read aloud in the reading view — proof-listening reveals stumbling points the eye skips. Test readers can have shared texts read to them too.
help.extra.citations.title: Citing
help.extra.citations.desc: Insert citations from your library into the text; every export builds the bibliography in the chosen citation style (APA 7, Chicago, numeric).
help.extra.evidence.title: Evidence suggestion
help.extra.evidence.desc: When copy-editing flags an unsupported sentence, the app searches the full texts of your sources for matching passages. One click adds the citation; the sentence stays unchanged.
help.extra.xrefs.title: Cross-references
help.extra.xrefs.desc: “See chapter 3”, “cf. fig. 3.2” as pointers instead of typed numbers. When you reorder, numbering follows, and every export writes the number valid there.
help.extra.diagrams.title: Diagrams
help.extra.diagrams.desc: Flowchart, sequence, timeline or mind map right in the text, in Mermaid syntax with live preview. The image is rendered fresh for every output.
help.extra.tables.title: Tables
help.extra.tables.desc: Insert tables via a grid with header row and column alignment. Typeset in the PDF, real tables in Word — with number and cross-reference.
help.extra.interview.title: Interview transcription
help.extra.interview.desc: An interview recording in the research board becomes a transcript with timestamps and speakers. In the reference panel you insert quotes into the article as cited block quotes.
help.extra.pageHistory.title: Section history
help.extra.pageHistory.desc: Below every section: earlier versions of the section and past copy-editing runs. View any version, compare it with the current one and restore it.
help.extra.kapitelReview.title: Chapter overview
help.extra.kapitelReview.desc: Overview of a single chapter — opened from the chapter in the sidebar: length, editing, style, characters, scenes and sections. Plus the chapter review, like the book review: grade per axis, strengths, weaknesses, improvements.
help.extra.researchChat.title: Research chat
help.extra.researchChat.desc: In the research board: a chat that searches the web and suggests finds with their source. You add what you like to the board with one click.
help.extra.plotChat.title: Plot chat
help.extra.plotChat.desc: In the plot workshop: a chat to develop the story in conversation. It knows the board, characters and text and suggests beats, acts and storylines. You apply each suggestion individually, and undo works like any board edit.
help.extra.ideenChat.title: Ideas chat
help.extra.ideenChat.desc: On the ideas board: a chat that checks your open items against the text. It reports what is already done (with the passage), finds a section for ideas without a place and spots duplicates. You apply each suggestion individually.
help.extra.imageGen.title: Image generation
help.extra.imageGen.desc: On request the book chat can generate images — character portrait, location, mood. Images stay in the chat and never enter the manuscript.
help.extra.comments.title: Test-reader comments
help.extra.comments.desc: Comments on shared links appear in a margin rail: for a section in its reading view, for chapters and books in the book editor. Reply, resolve and delete there.
help.extra.collab.title: Collaboration
help.extra.collab.desc: Invite members in the book settings as viewer, copy-editor, editor or owner. You see who is working on what; a section being edited is locked for others.
help.extra.blogSync.title: Blog sync
help.extra.blogSync.desc: Sync blog-type books with WordPress or HubSpot: import posts, transfer changes both ways, publish. The connection lives in the book settings.
help.extra.userSettings.title: Profile & settings
help.extra.userSettings.desc: In the avatar menu: interface language, daily goal, defaults for new books, focus editor behaviour, personal dictionary, devices, app downloads and account.
help.extra.palette.title: Command palette
help.extra.palette.desc: ⌘K / Ctrl+K or / opens the palette: find any card, section, character or location by typing and jump straight there.
help.extra.extension.title: Browser extension
help.extra.extension.desc: The Chrome extension saves the open web page as a research find or source with one click, reading title, author and access date by itself.
help.extra.nativeApps.title: Mac and Android apps
help.extra.nativeApps.desc: Write offline too: the focus editor as an app for macOS and Android, with the same login. Changes sync the next time you connect.

pdfExport.layout.hfSidesHint: Right-hand pages (recto) are the baseline and apply everywhere. Fill in left-hand pages (verso) only if they should differ (e.g. book title on the left, chapter on the right) — empty fields reuse the right-hand page.
pdfExport.layout.pageNumberStartHint: The number the first counted page carries — this is the lever for the numbering's start value. “Body pages only”: the first body page (e.g. 1 → first body page shows “1”). “All pages”: the first PDF page.
pdfExport.layout.pageNumberFirstVisibleH: A lower bound, not a start value: pages with a smaller counted number stay without a footer number. It can only push the first visible number later, never earlier — the start value is set by “Page numbering starts at”. It counts the body page (front matter/blank pages don't count), so the number appears later in the PDF.

A lower bound, not a start value: pages with a smaller number stay without a footer number. It can only push the first visible number later, never earlier. Since all pages are counted, the value matches the PDF page; a value below the first body page's number has no effect — for a smaller start value, choose “Body pages only”.
pdfExport.layout.pageCountModeHintBody: Count body pages only. Front matter (cover, title, table of contents) and inserted blank pages carry no number and are not counted — so the printed number is lower than the PDF page (book convention).
pdfExport.layout.pageCountModeHintPhysic: All physical pages are counted: front matter and blank pages each consume a number (without showing it), so the printed number matches the PDF page.
pdfExport.layout.frontMatterNumberingHin: Separate numbering for title/dedication/epigraph/table of contents. The cover never gets a number.
pdfExport.layout.frontMatterNumberFirstV: Front matter number visible from page
Lower bound for the separate front matter numbering: earlier front matter pages are counted but show no number. Affects only the front matter, not the body pages.
pdfExport.layout.mirrorMarginsHint: When active: left margin = gutter (inner) on right-hand pages, swapped on left-hand pages. Header/footer mirror accordingly.
pdfExport.layout.hyphenateHint: Breaks long words in justified text using DE/EN hyphenation patterns. Reduces rivers and large word gaps.
pdfExport.layout.widowOrphanHint: Prevents single trailing or leading lines stranded at the top/bottom of the next page. Measures paragraph height before printing and pushes the whole paragraph to the next page when necessary.

admin.settings.stt.host.help: Base URL without path, e.g. http://whisper.local:8000. The /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint is appended automatically.
admin.settings.stt.model.label: Model
admin.settings.stt.model.help: Model ID of the Whisper server.
admin.settings.stt.apiKey.label: API key (optional)
admin.settings.stt.apiKey.help: Optional bearer token for hosted endpoints. Empty = no Authorization header (local servers).
admin.settings.stt.language.label: Fallback language
admin.settings.stt.language.help: Only used when there is no book scope. Otherwise the book language wins.
admin.settings.stt.temperature.label: Temperature
admin.settings.stt.temperature.help: Sampling temperature of the Whisper model. Range 0–1, default 0 (deterministic, fewer hallucinations).
admin.settings.stt.upstreamTimeoutMs.hel: Maximum wait for the Whisper endpoint per segment. Choose generously so a GPU cold start (model reload after idle) does not lose the segment to a timeout. Range 5000–120000 ms, default 30000.
admin.settings.stt.vadSilenceMs.label: VAD silence (ms)
admin.settings.stt.vadSilenceMs.help: Duration of the speech pause after which a segment is cut and transcribed. Range 200–5000 ms, default 800.
admin.settings.stt.vadThreshold.label: VAD threshold
admin.settings.stt.vadThreshold.help: RMS volume threshold for speech vs. silence. Range 0–1, default 0.015.
admin.settings.stt.vadMaxSegmentS.label: Max. segment length (s)
admin.settings.stt.vadMaxSegmentS.help: Forces a cut during continuous speech without a pause. Range 5–120 s, default 30.
admin.settings.tts.hint: Self-hosted text-to-speech (OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint, e.g. Kokoro-FastAPI / openedai-speech). Adds a read-aloud button in the notebook editor that reads the text sentence by sentence and highlights the current one. Audio is only proxied, never stored; host/key never leave the server.
admin.settings.tts.enabled.label: Read-aloud active
admin.settings.tts.host.label: Speech host URL
admin.settings.tts.host.help: Base URL without path, e.g. http://tts.local:8880. The /v1/audio/speech endpoint is appended automatically.
admin.settings.tts.model.label: Model
admin.settings.tts.model.help: Model ID of the speech server.
admin.settings.tts.voice.label: Default voice
admin.settings.tts.voice.help: Voice ID of the server. Fallback when no language-specific voice is set for the book language.
admin.settings.tts.voiceDe.label: Voice German
admin.settings.tts.voiceEn.label: Voice English
admin.settings.tts.voiceLocale.help: Optional. Used for books in this language; empty = default voice.
admin.settings.tts.format.label: Audio format
admin.settings.tts.format.help: Container of the synthesized audio. MP3 is the most widely compatible; older Safari versions cannot play Opus.
admin.settings.tts.speed.label: Speed
admin.settings.tts.pauseFragmentMs.label: Pause between fragments (ms)
admin.settings.tts.pauseFragmentMs.help: Breathing pause between read-out fragments (sentence to sentence). Range 0–5000, default 250. 0 = no pause.
admin.settings.tts.pauseParagraphMs.help: Breathing pause at paragraph boundaries, usually a bit longer than between fragments. Range 0–5000, default 550. 0 = no pause.
admin.settings.tts.apiKey.label: API key (optional)
admin.settings.tts.apiKey.help: Optional bearer token for hosted endpoints. Empty = no Authorization header (local servers).
admin.settings.image.hint: Self-hosted image generation (OpenAI-compatible image endpoint, e.g. a ComfyUI/SD-WebUI/Flux bridge, vLLM). Enables an image-generation tool in the agentic book chat (Claude provider only). Generated images are pure visualization in the chat history and never enter the book text; host/key never leave the server.
admin.settings.image.enabled.label: Enable image generation
admin.settings.image.host.label: Host
admin.settings.image.host.help: Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The path /v1/images/generations is appended automatically.
admin.settings.image.model.label: Model
admin.settings.image.model.help: Model name sent to the endpoint. Empty = server default.
admin.settings.image.size.label: Image size
admin.settings.image.size.help: Default format as WIDTHxHEIGHT. The AI may override it per image.
admin.settings.image.timeoutMs.label: Timeout (ms)
admin.settings.image.timeoutMs.help: Maximum wait per image generation. Diffusion models often need 30–120 s.
admin.settings.image.apiKey.label: API key (optional)
admin.settings.image.apiKey.help: Optional bearer token for hosted endpoints. Empty = no Authorization header (local servers).
admin.settings.embed.hint: Self-hosted embedding endpoint (OpenAI-compatible, /v1/embeddings, e.g. LocalAI) for semantic search. Enables the meaning-based search mode, the “Similar passages” buttons on figures/scenes and the book-chat tool search_similar. Provider-independent (its own endpoint, not the chat provider). Host/model/key never leave the server. After enabling, build the index per book (search card).
admin.settings.embed.enabled.label: Enable semantic search
admin.settings.embed.host.label: Host
admin.settings.embed.host.help: Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The path /v1/embeddings is appended automatically.
admin.settings.embed.model.label: Model
admin.settings.embed.model.help: Embedding model. bge-m3 recommended: multilingual, 8k context, 1024 dimensions. Changing the model requires rebuilding the index.
admin.settings.embed.dim.label: Dimensions
admin.settings.embed.dim.help: Vector length of the model (bge-m3 = 1024). Must match the model; used as a sanity check against the actually returned length.
admin.settings.embed.timeoutMs.label: Timeout (ms)
admin.settings.embed.timeoutMs.help: Maximum wait per embedding batch. A GPU cold start (model reload after idle) can delay the first request.
admin.settings.embed.autoindexDelay.help: After this many seconds without further changes to a book, the index is updated (only changed text is re-embedded). 0 = off, nightly run only.
admin.settings.embed.apiKey.label: API key (optional)
admin.settings.embed.apiKey.help: Optional bearer token for hosted endpoints. Empty = no Authorization header (local servers).
admin.settings.embed.qualityHint: Tuning for free-text search. The score floor drops weak hits; hybrid fusion blends in full-text search. The instruction prefixes are only needed by asymmetric models (e.g. e5) — leave empty for bge-m3.
admin.settings.embed.minScore.label: Minimum similarity (score floor)
admin.settings.embed.minScore.help: Cosine floor for free-text hits (0–1). Similarity search never returns "no results" — this cuts the weak long tail. bge-m3: relevant passages usually score above 0.4; 0 = off. Does not apply to "similar passages" buttons (recall matters there).
admin.settings.embed.hybrid.label: Hybrid search (combine full-text + meaning)
admin.settings.embed.queryPrefix.label: Query prefix
admin.settings.embed.queryPrefix.help: Instruction prefix prepended to every search query (asymmetric models like e5 require "query: "). Leave empty for bge-m3.
admin.settings.embed.passagePrefix.label: Passage prefix
admin.settings.embed.passagePrefix.help: Instruction prefix for the indexed passages (e5: "passage: "). Changing it forces an index rebuild. Leave empty for bge-m3.
admin.settings.plotAnchor.title: Plot anchoring
admin.settings.plotAnchor.hint: Matches popover + drift badge of the plot workshop.
admin.settings.figurAnchor.title: Figure anchoring
admin.settings.figurAnchor.hint: Arc band + arc findings of the figure workshop.
admin.settings.plotAnchorMinScore.label: Minimum match similarity (score floor)
admin.settings.plotAnchorMinScore.help: Cosine floor (0–1) for a beat's matches in the text. Weak semantic hits are hidden from the popover and the drift badge — takes effect immediately, no need to re-run anchoring. Literal full-text hits always stay visible. 0 = show all.
admin.settings.plotAnchorConfirmMinScore: Confirmation threshold for "in the book" beats

Cosine floor (0–1) above which a semantic match confirms a beat marked "in the book". Similarity search finds a nearest neighbour for every beat — without a threshold almost every beat would count as confirmed and the drift badge would stay silent. Applied during the anchoring run (weaker matches are not stored for "in the book" beats). Literal full-text matches without an embedding backend are unaffected. 0 = every semantic match counts.
admin.settings.plotAnchorPromoteMinScore: Cosine floor (0–1) above which a PLANNED beat counts as "apparently already written" and gets a promotion badge ("Mark as in the book?"). Deliberately high — otherwise nearly every planned beat would produce weak hits and flood the board with false suggestions. Applied during the anchoring run (only stronger matches are stored for planned beats). 0 = promotion detection off.
admin.settings.motifScan.title: Motif detection
admin.settings.motifScan.hint: Occurrence list + actual density of the motif workshop.
admin.settings.motif.scanMinScore.label: Minimum occurrence similarity (score floor)
admin.settings.motif.scanMinScore.help: Cosine floor (0–1) for a motif's occurrences in the text. Unlikely semantic hits are hidden from the panel list, confidence %, and actual density (node size + ghost detection) — takes effect immediately, no need to re-run the motif scan. Literal trigger hits always stay visible. 0 = show all.
admin.settings.redundancy.title: Redundancy radar
admin.settings.redundancy.hint: Cosine thresholds for the three sensitivity bands the redundancy radar (book-wide duplication scan) runs over the embedding index. Model-dependent — the defaults are calibrated for bge-m3; adjust here for a different embedding model. Higher value = stricter (only very similar passages). Allowed range is 0.70–0.97. The bands also colour the score badges in the result.
admin.settings.redundancy.thresholdLoose: Also surfaces merely thematically close passages. Default 0.76.
admin.settings.rerank.title: Reranker (cross-encoder)
admin.settings.rerank.hint: Optional second stage: a cross-encoder re-orders the free-text hits of semantic search by comparing query and passage directly (sharper relevance than vector distance alone). Self-hosted, OpenAI/Jina-compatible /v1/rerank endpoint (e.g. LocalAI, TEI). Requires semantic search to be enabled. If the endpoint fails, the normal order is used silently.
admin.settings.rerank.enabled.label: Enable reranking
admin.settings.rerank.host.label: Host
admin.settings.rerank.host.help: Base URL of the OpenAI/Jina-compatible endpoint. The /v1/rerank path is appended automatically.
admin.settings.rerank.model.label: Model
admin.settings.rerank.model.help: Reranker model. bge-reranker-v2-m3 recommended: multilingual, pairs with bge-m3.
admin.settings.rerank.topN.label: Candidates (top-N)
admin.settings.rerank.topN.help: How many of the best retrieval hits the reranker re-scores. Higher = more thorough, but slower and costlier per search.
admin.settings.rerank.batchSize.label: Batch size
admin.settings.rerank.batchSize.help: How many passages go to the reranker per request; larger candidate pools are split into batches. Must fit the backend limit (HuggingFace TEI: --max-client-batch-size, default 32).
admin.settings.rerank.minScore.label: Minimum relevance
admin.settings.rerank.minScore.help: Relevance floor after reranking (0–1). 0 = keep all. Scale depends on the model (bge-reranker returns values around 0..1).
admin.settings.rerank.timeoutMs.label: Timeout (ms)
admin.settings.rerank.timeoutMs.help: Maximum wait per rerank call. On timeout the normal hit order is used silently.
admin.settings.rerank.apiKey.label: API key (optional)
admin.settings.rerank.apiKey.help: Optional bearer token for hosted endpoints. Empty = no Authorization header (local servers).
admin.settings.geocode.hint: Source for the locations map's coordinate lookup. Nominatim (OSM) runs public or self-hosted; Photon (Komoot) is self-hosted. No hit = manual pin via marker drag is always possible.
admin.settings.geocode.provider.label: Provider
admin.settings.geocode.nominatim.label: Nominatim URL
admin.settings.geocode.nominatim.help: Full search endpoint. Public instance: max. 1 request/second (serialized server-side). Self-hosted has no limit.
admin.settings.geocode.photon.label: Photon URL
admin.settings.geocode.photon.help: Base URL of the Photon instance without path (e.g. http://photon.lan:2322). The /api endpoint is appended automatically.
admin.settings.geocode.tilesHint: Source of the map imagery. Leaflet fetches the tiles directly in the browser. Default = public OSM (mind the tile usage policy); your own tile server takes load off the public OSM servers and fits the self-hosting philosophy.
admin.settings.geocode.tiles.label: Tile server URL
admin.settings.geocode.tiles.help: Map tile URL in {z}/{x}/{y}.png scheme (Leaflet fetches tiles directly in the browser). Clear the field and it falls back to the public OSM server (https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png) — then mind the OSM tile usage policy. Self-hosted tile server (e.g. openstreetmap-tile-server or tileserver-gl): enter your own URL, many serve under /tile/ — example: http://tiles.lan:8080/tile/{z}/{x}/{y}.png. The {s} subdomain is optional. An http://-only tile server (e.g. on your LAN) is automatically served through the app's own proxy — it needs neither HTTPS nor to be exposed.
Copyright notice shown at the bottom-right of the map. Empty = default OSM attribution. Adjust for a self-hosted tile server.
admin.settings.analytics.scriptUrlHint: Full URL to the Plausible tracker JS, e.g. https://analytics.example.com/js/pa-XXXX.js. The origin is added to the CSP automatically. Tracking runs on every host as soon as the checkbox is enabled.
admin.settings.smtp.hint: Gmail account for invite + notification mails. Active as soon as address and App Password are set. Host/port/TLS are implicit via service:'gmail' (smtp.gmail.com:465 TLS).
admin.settings.smtp.appPasswordHint: 2FA must be enabled. Generate the 16-character app password at:
admin.settings.mail.adminRecipientHint: Forwarding address for admin notifications (job crash, token cap, budget overrun). Empty = sent to all active admin users. Set = replaces that list entirely; the address does not need to match an app account.
admin.settings.mail.notifyHint: Master toggles per notification path. Only effective when SMTP is configured.
admin.settings.mail.skipErrorsHint: Comma-separated list of error/i18n keys that do NOT trigger a crash mail. Empty = defaults from lib/notify.js.
admin.settings.auth.captchaHint: Self-hosted proof-of-work captcha (no third party). Protects /register and the ENV admin login against bots. Active = the browser invisibly solves a compute puzzle on submit; the HMAC secret is generated automatically when enabled. The hard rate limits stay active regardless.
admin.settings.help.altchaComplexity: Difficulty of the compute puzzle (upper search bound). Higher = more bot cost, but a slightly slower solve in the browser. Default 100,000.
admin.settings.help.altchaChallengeTtl: Lifetime of an issued ALTCHA challenge in minutes. Long enough for slow devices, short enough to keep the replay window tight. Default 10.
admin.settings.auth.rateLimitHint: In-memory per IP, independent of the ALTCHA protection. Register: max requests per window (minutes), then 429. Admin login: after max failed attempts per window the IP is blocked for the same period. Counters reset on server restart.
admin.settings.help.registrationExpireDa: Maximum age of pending registration requests in days. After that the cron marks them 'expired'.
admin.settings.help.appName: Display name of the app (mail templates, landing page, startup log).
admin.settings.help.seoIndexable: Off: robots.txt blocks everything and the landing/privacy pages carry noindex again. For secondary instances (demo, staging) that would otherwise enter the search index as duplicates of the main domain. Requires a configured public base URL — without one the instance stays unindexed regardless of this switch. Shared content is always excluded.
admin.settings.models.error: Could not fetch the model list ({err}).
admin.settings.advanced.disclaimer: Leave defaults unless you have a strong reason — values are calibrated from practice.
admin.profiles.intro: Named model configurations that can be assigned to individual people in the users tab. Every field left empty inherits from the matching provider tab — so a profile only carries what should really differ, and global changes keep flowing through. Without a profile, a person follows the globally configured provider.
admin.profiles.col.name: Name
admin.profiles.empty: No profiles yet. Without a profile everyone follows the globally configured provider.
admin.profiles.field.name: Name
admin.profiles.keyHelp: Leave empty: when creating, the provider's global key applies; when editing, the stored key stays. The key is stored encrypted and never returned.
admin.profiles.maxParallelHelp: Applies to this profile only: every endpoint has its own counter, so a local server is not swamped by a hosted one's limit.
admin.profiles.confirmDeleteUsers: Delete profile “{name}”? {n} person(s) lose the assignment and will follow the globally configured provider again.
admin.settings.help.providerChoice: Default provider for users without their own override. Per-user override in user management.
admin.settings.help.appTimezone: IANA time zone (e.g. Europe/Zurich). Applies to cron jobs, server date buckets (streak, page_stats), and all GUI date formatters — browser time zone is overridden.
admin.settings.help.contextWindow: Full model context window (input + output) in tokens. For local models, set this to the native context size (Mistral-Small3.2 / Gemma3 / Llama-3.1: 128 000; older: 32 000 / 8 000).
admin.settings.help.maxTokensOut: Output cap in tokens. Must be well below `context_window` (the rest = input budget). Per-job overrides are capped on top.
admin.settings.komplett.title: Impact on the full analysis
admin.settings.komplett.derived: Derived from this: single-pass up to {single} characters, otherwise split into chunks of {chunk} characters (input budget {budget} characters).
admin.settings.komplett.warn: Recommended for the full analysis: at least {recommended} tokens of context window. With {ctx} tokens a longer book gets split into small chunks — characters, facts and continuity are fragmented across many passes, which lowers extraction quality.
admin.settings.komplett.bad: {ctx} tokens of context window is very tight for the full analysis: even short books are shredded into tiny chunks of {chunk} characters, and relationships and continuity across chapter boundaries are lost. At least {recommended} tokens strongly recommended (the native size of modern local models such as Mistral-Small3.2 / Gemma3 / Llama-3.1).
admin.settings.help.repeatPenalty: Anti-loop: penalises recently repeated tokens and breaks repetition loops (e.g. during JSON extraction). 1.0 = off, 1.1–1.2 mild recommended. Values too high can damage valid JSON.
admin.settings.help.think: Enable reasoning/thinking. Off (recommended): the model does not think, saving output tokens. On: models like Qwen3 or DeepSeek-R1 emit a reasoning trace that we discard — costs tokens and time.
admin.settings.help.thinkOpenaiCompat: Enable reasoning/thinking. Off (recommended): sends `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` to suppress the reasoning trace on vLLM/SGLang/llama.cpp (Qwen3 & co), saving output tokens. On: nothing is sent (model default) — use this for real OpenAI, which rejects unknown fields.
admin.settings.help.maxParallelOpenaiCom: Maximum number of concurrent calls to the server. 1 = strictly serial (like Ollama). Set higher if the local server can handle parallel requests (e.g. LocalAI with multiple slots); excess calls wait in a queue.
admin.settings.openaiCompat.komplettIntr: Applies only to the full-analysis family (extraction, consolidation, continuity). Empty field / 0 = follows the standard values above. Lets the book analysis run on a stronger model with a larger window, while standard calls (editing, chat) stay on the everyday model.
admin.settings.openaiCompat.bookchatIntr: For the book chat only (classic + agentic tool loop). Empty field / 0 = follows the defaults above. Useful because the chat needs the inverse shape of the full analysis: lots of input (tool catalogue, initial context, growing tool results — paid again every iteration without caching), little output. An output cap set for the analysis otherwise eats the chat's input budget.
admin.settings.help.komplettModelOpenaiC: Model used only for the full analysis. Empty = follows the standard model above. Useful when the same endpoint serves several models and the book analysis should get a stronger one than editing and chat.
admin.settings.help.komplettContextWindo: Context window for the full analysis only. 0 = follows the standard value above. Higher = larger books run single-pass (more accurate). Must match the model the endpoint actually loads.
admin.settings.help.komplettMaxTokensOut: Output cap for the full analysis only. 0 = follows the standard value above. Must stay well below the context window, otherwise there is no room left for the input.
admin.settings.help.komplettTimeoutMsOpe: Hard timeout per call for the full analysis only (milliseconds). 0 = follows the standard timeout above. The book analysis makes several very large calls and often needs more than the usual 600000 (10 min). Example: 2400000 = 40 min.
admin.settings.help.timeoutMsOpenaiCompa: Hard timeout per call (milliseconds). Without it a silent endpoint — a stalled stream, a provider outage — holds the job indefinitely. User cancellation is unaffected.
admin.settings.help.retryMaxOpenaiCompat: Number of attempts on transient server responses (408, 429, 5xx) with increasing backoff. Deterministic errors (400, 401, 404) are not retried.
admin.settings.help.cloudOpenaiCompat: Model class of the endpoint. Off (default): weak/local model — slimmed prompts, one combined proofreading call, serial processing. On: hosted frontier model (e.g. Kimi/Moonshot, OpenAI) — full cloud prompts incl. JSON enforcement, focused proofreading passes (if split is enabled), parallel calls (capped by max. parallel). Claude-exclusive features (prompt caching, research chat, continuity verify, tiered routing) are unaffected.
admin.settings.help.openaiCompatApiKey: Optional bearer token for hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints (vLLM, LiteLLM, OpenAI). Leave empty for local servers without auth (e.g. llama.cpp).
admin.settings.help.komplettExtractMaxTo: Output-token limit for the full-analysis AI calls (extraction, consolidation, continuity). Effective only for local models (Ollama / openai-compat) — caps their generation length to protect VRAM/latency. Ignored when `ai.provider = claude` (Claude caps at the provider ceiling since only generated tokens are billed).
admin.settings.help.claudeMaxTokensOut: Output cap in tokens. 0 = derived from the model. Must be clearly smaller than the context window.
admin.settings.help.claudeContextWindow: Total context window (input + output) in tokens. 0 = derived from the model.
admin.settings.help.claudeModel: Model for all Claude calls (proofreading, chats, reviews, full analysis). Different models per job can be set under “Advanced”.
admin.settings.claude.limitsIntro: 0 = derived from the model (Opus 4.7+/Sonnet 5+/Fable: 1M context, 128K output; older models: 200K / 64K). Only set these to deviate on purpose. Retries, timeout and concurrency control behaviour against Anthropic TPM limits.
admin.settings.claude.advancedIntro: Everything here is optional. Empty fields or 0 follow the standard above: the same model for all jobs, context window and output limit derived from the model.
admin.settings.help.komplettModel: Claude model used only for the full analysis (extraction, consolidation, continuity). Empty = follows `ai.claude.model`. Lets you run e.g. Opus for the more thorough book analysis while Sonnet stays global (e.g. for editing). Only applies when `ai.provider = claude`.
admin.settings.help.komplettModelExtract: Separate Claude model for the raw-text extraction calls of the full analysis only (full extraction, completeness gaps, coverage feedback/audit, life events), while consolidation + continuity judgement run on `ai.claude.model.komplett`. Empty = no tiering. Caution, recall-critical: gaps and coverage feedback add missing figures/locations to the catalog, so this is not pure diagnostics — a weak model (e.g. Haiku) noticeably lowers recall here, especially across the long tail of minor characters. So the point is not cheaper extraction but a stronger consolidation model above (e.g. claude-opus-4-8[1m]) with normal extraction here (claude-sonnet-5); do not go weaker than Sonnet. Only applies when `ai.provider = claude`.
admin.settings.help.komplettContextWindo: Context window for the full analysis only. 0 = follows `ai.claude.context_window`. Higher = larger books run single-pass (more accurate). Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.x support up to 1000000.
admin.settings.help.komplettMaxTokensOut: Output cap for the full analysis only. 0 = follows `ai.claude.max_tokens_out`. Must match the full-analysis model: Sonnet 4.6 ≤ 64000, Opus 4.8 ≤ 128000 — too high returns HTTP 400. Lets the analysis use more output on Opus without the global (e.g. Sonnet) calls exceeding the 64K limit.
admin.settings.help.komplettTimeoutMs: Hard timeout per Claude call for the full analysis only (milliseconds). 0 = follows `ai.claude.timeout_ms`. Opus is slower and the single-pass makes several large calls — so the book analysis often needs more than the global 600000 (10 min). Example: 2400000 = 40 min. Max 3600000 (60 min).
admin.settings.help.bookchatModel: Claude model used only for the book chat. Empty = follows `ai.claude.model`. Lets you run e.g. Opus for the agentic tool loop while Sonnet stays global (e.g. for editing). Only applies when `ai.provider = claude`.
admin.settings.help.bookchatContextWindo: Context window for the book chat only. 0 = follows `ai.claude.context_window`. Higher = more book text / tool results per answer. Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.x support up to 1000000.
admin.settings.help.bookchatMaxTokensOut: Output cap for the book chat only. 0 = follows `ai.claude.max_tokens_out`. Must match the book-chat model: Sonnet 4.6 ≤ 64000, Opus 4.8 ≤ 128000 — too high returns HTTP 400.
admin.settings.help.bookchatTimeoutMs: Hard timeout per Claude call for the book chat only (milliseconds). 0 = follows `ai.claude.timeout_ms`. The global 10-min default is usually enough (one tool-use round per call). Max 3600000 (60 min).
admin.settings.help.completenessPasses: Claude only: how many extra passes after the first extraction specifically hunt for missed characters, locations, facts and scenes (long-tail recall). Applies to single-pass AND multi-pass (large books, per chunk). 0 = off. Stops early once a round finds nothing new. Higher = more thorough, but more tokens/time.
admin.settings.help.coverageAuditChapter: Claude only: coverage self-audit. After consolidation, N random chapters are checked for named characters/locations missing from the catalog → recall score in the job result. Runs on the extraction tier (cheap). 0 = off.
admin.settings.help.coverageMinScore: Threshold (0–1) below which the coverage score is reported as a warning in the job result. Default 0.8.
admin.settings.help.attributeCheck: Claude only: attribute contradiction detector. Finds contradictory values of the same attribute across chapters (from life events + world facts) and lets the model judge the candidates — augments the continuity check with cross-chapter contradictions.
admin.settings.help.entityMatchJudge: Claude only: when reconciling the catalogue, uncertain pairs (similar name, but not clearly the same character / location / scene) are put to the model for a decision — only the suspected pairs, not the whole list. Off: uncertain pairs stay separate and show up as “no longer in the text” duplicates that you merge by hand in the book settings.
admin.settings.help.komplettEffort: Claude only, full analysis only: effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) for all analysis calls. Empty = no effort field (API default high). On Opus 4.7+/Sonnet 5 e.g. xhigh for the most demanding judgement/verify phases. Invalid values are ignored; on models without effort support it silently clamps to high. Note: effort tokens (adaptive thinking) count against the same output budget as the JSON.
admin.settings.help.lektoratEffort: Claude only, section and batch proofreading only: effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Applies only to models with adaptive thinking (Sonnet 5+, Opus 4.7+, Fable/Mythos); on Sonnet 4.6 and older no effort field is sent. Empty = the model's default (high, medium on Opus 5.5) — the model then often thinks silently for several minutes per section and output costs multiply. low is fastest but finds noticeably less. The value feeds the proofreading cache version.
admin.settings.help.reviewEffort: Claude only, book and chapter review only: effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Applies only to models with adaptive thinking (Sonnet 5+, Opus 4.7+, Fable/Mythos). Empty = the model's default (Opus 5.5: medium, older: high). Default high, because judging a whole book depends on reasoning depth. The value feeds the review cache version.
admin.settings.help.synonymEffort: Claude only, AI synonym search only: effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Applies only to models with adaptive thinking. Default low — a word list needs little reasoning depth, any higher level only lengthens the wait in the context menu. Empty = the model's default (Sonnet 5.5: high, Opus 5.5: medium). The value feeds the synonym cache version.
admin.settings.help.synonymModel: Claude model for the AI synonym search only. Empty = follows `ai.claude.model`. A fast model such as claude-sonnet-5-5 is recommended: in measurements roughly half the wait of Opus 5.5 and a third of the cost, with equivalent suggestions. Changing it invalidates the synonym cache. Only applies when `ai.provider = claude`.
admin.settings.help.lektoratModel: Claude model used only for section and batch proofreading. Empty = follows `ai.claude.model`. Lets you run e.g. a thinking model such as Opus 5.5 for proofreading while section chat and reviews stay on the global model. The effort below only applies if this model uses adaptive thinking. Changing it invalidates the proofreading cache. Only applies when `ai.provider = claude`.
admin.settings.help.extractSinglePassCap: Claude only: decouples the extraction threshold from the continuity threshold (characters). 0 = off (extraction follows the context window). With a large window (Opus 4.8 + 1M) almost every book would otherwise run single-pass — good for the continuity check, worse for extraction (long-tail recall + output budget). >0 forces extraction into per-chapter chunks (better completeness) while continuity/narrative profile still see the whole book. Recommended for Opus 4.8 + 1M: ~700000.
admin.settings.help.figureBatchSize: Claude only: character batch size for the life-events (E) and relationships (A2) passes. Large casts are queried in groups of this size in parallel (smaller, more robust outputs, less truncation). ≤ cast size = 1 call (as before for small books). Default 20.
admin.settings.help.sceneBackfillMinChar: Claude only: from how many characters a chapter counts as "substantial" for scene backfill (chapters with ≥ this much text but 0 extracted scenes get a targeted scene follow-up call). Default 3000.
admin.settings.help.timelineConsolidateM: Above how many timeline events the cosmetic AI polish is skipped for local models. Events are then stored pre-grouped — complete, just without dedup and unified phrasing. At 20–30 tokens/s this call takes tens of minutes once there are a few hundred events. 0 = no cap. Does not affect cloud models.
admin.settings.help.sceneBackfill: Claude only: chapters with substantial text for which extraction returned no scene get a targeted scene follow-up call. Deterministic gap detection, only the fix needs AI.
admin.settings.help.remapRescue: Claude only: before unresolvable character names from scenes/events are dropped, a cheap resolution call maps nicknames/partial names/variants to the catalog — rescuing scene-character links and event assignments. Runs only if there are unresolvable names at all.
admin.settings.help.factcheck: Claude only: enables the world-fact fact check (a separate job per book). Extracted world facts are checked against real-world facts via web search. Costs one web search per fact — off by default on purpose. Additionally enable it per book in the book settings.
admin.settings.help.charsPerToken: Scales char-to-token estimates. Provider-agnostic. Default 3.0 is calibrated for German.
admin.settings.label.jobsResearchChatMax: Research chat: max web searches per answer
admin.settings.label.komplettSceneBackfi: Full analysis: scene backfill min chars
admin.settings.label.komplettTimelineCon: Timeline consolidation up to max. events (local)
admin.settings.label.lektoratStylisticCa: Proofreading: max. style findings per 10,000 characters
admin.settings.help.lektoratSplit: Claude only: splits section editing into focused passes — one objective pass (spelling, grammar, punctuation, dialogue format, figure consistency) and one style pass (style, scenes, verdict). Focused passes yield more precise and complete findings than one big combined call, at the cost of more calls. Off = one combined call. Local models always run one combined call.
admin.settings.help.lektoratStylisticCap: Upper limit for subjective style findings (style, sentence structure, repetition, filler words …) per 10,000 characters of section text. Long sections get proportionally more (at most five times this value, max. 200), short ones never fewer than this value. It is part of the prompt – the model then keeps the most severe ones – and is also enforced on the server, spread across the whole section. Spelling, grammar and consistency do not count towards it and are never capped. Default 10.
admin.settings.help.lektoratObjectiveRun: Only when split is on: number of parallel runs of the objective pass (spelling, grammar, punctuation, dialogue format, figure consistency). Agreeing findings are kept by consensus, which filters out run-to-run unstable one-offs and raises precision. 1 = a single objective run without consensus. Local models always run exactly one pass.
admin.settings.help.lektoratConsensusThr: An objective finding is kept only if at least this many objective passes report it. Higher = stricter and more precise but fewer findings; a value equal to the number of runs requires unanimity (maximum precision). Clamped to the number of runs.
admin.settings.help.pageRevisionLimit: Floor for section-revisions retention: newest N revisions per section are always kept on top of the GFS schema (24h / 1 per day / 1 per week / 1 per month / 1 per year, oldest of each). Cleanup runs daily.
admin.settings.help.editorLockTtl: Lifetime of a section lock (lektorat mutex + edit hint) in minutes without a heartbeat. After that the lock expires and the section becomes editable again. Default 30.
admin.settings.help.shareCommentRateLimi: Beta-reader comments via share links: max comments per token + IP per window (minutes), then 429. Generous enough for many inline annotations per session. In-memory, resets on server restart.
admin.settings.help.macclientGithubToken: Optional GitHub token (PAT) for fetching client versions in the profile: Android app and Chrome extension (the macOS app comes from the Mac App Store and does not need it). Empty = unauthenticated (60 requests/h per IP). Set = raises the rate limit (5000/h). Does not fix network timeouts.

finetune.title: Fine-tuning export
finetune.lead: Generates JSONL training data from book text, characters, events, scenes, and locations. Chat format (messages) plus optional pre-rendered Tekken-V7 text field, loads directly in Unsloth Studio or the Unsloth CLI. Defaults tuned for Mistral-Small-3.2-24B (131072-token context, full-chapter samples enabled). For QLoRA on 20-24 GB set max_seq_tokens to 4096.
finetune.type.style.desc: Paragraph start → continuation. Many samples, teaches the author's tone.
finetune.type.scene.desc: Metadata (characters · location · chapter) → scene text, plus full-chapter completions, sliding-window cuts (start/middle/end), multi-section and chapter-to-chapter continuations, and cloze fill-ins. Uses full-analysis data.
finetune.type.verbatim.desc: Section/chapter → exact full text, uncut and chunked at sentence boundaries. Strongest memorization type: forces the model to learn the book text word for word.
finetune.type.dialog.desc: Character + context → dialogue line. Heuristically extracted from quotes.
finetune.type.authorChat.desc: "Chat with author and book": questions about characters (incl. roleplay, comparison, single fields), events (causal chains, chronology, POV), scenes (POV generation, reverse lookup), locations (incl. journey sequences), themes + real book-chat history.
finetune.type.correction.desc: Original → improved sentence from all past editing runs. Trains the editorial eye in the author's voice.
finetune.bias.desc: Multiplies the per-character/per-section caps (dialogue, sentences, facts, passages). Higher = more redundant samples per source = stronger memorization bias, but higher overfitting risk. Training epochs have the biggest effect, not this value.
finetune.balance.desc: Caps each sample type to this fraction of the total (guideline: 0.4 ≈ 40% per type). Dampens the high-volume text samplers (style/scene/verbatim) so world and character knowledge (author chat, AI Q&A) is not drowned out. Selection is deterministic (seed-stable).
finetune.valSplit.desc: Split is per chapter: all samples from one chapter go together into train or val. This makes val a true holdout, so eval loss measures generalization rather than memorized training text. With few chapters the val share may fluctuate.
finetune.unsloth.maxSeqTokens: Max tokens per sample (0 = no filter)
finetune.unsloth.emitText.desc: Adds a text field next to messages, pre-rendered with the Mistral Tekken-V7 chat template (Mistral-Small-3.2). Lets you use SFTTrainer(dataset_text_field="text") without a formatting_func.
finetune.unsloth.truncateLong: Truncate long samples instead of dropping
finetune.unsloth.truncateLong.desc: Samples over the token limit are cut at sentence boundary instead of being discarded. More training data, occasional mid-sentence cuts possible.
finetune.ai.lead: Multiplies sample variety with AI-generated user prompts. Answers stay original text or structured DB fields — no AI-style prose in the training output. Cached per book and model.
finetune.ai.reversePrompts.desc: Generates several natural instructions/questions per section that lead to the existing section text. Multiplies variation without inventing new text.
finetune.ai.factQA.desc: Grounded question–answer pairs per character and location, derived from DB profiles. Trains world knowledge explicitly.
finetune.ai.reasoningBackfill.desc: Where editing entries lack a reason, fill in a one-sentence explanation. Promotes more corrections into the reasoned variant.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Protecting your data matters to us. This policy describes which data is processed when operating the service, for what purpose, and which rights you have.
privacy.sec1Body: The controller responsible for data processing is David Berger, Basel, Switzerland, bede.berger@gmail.com. As a Swiss operator, processing is governed by the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP); for users in the EU, the GDPR additionally applies.
privacy.sec2Intro: We only process data that is necessary to operate the service:
privacy.sec2ItemA: Account data: email address, display name and details from the access request, including where the request came from (referring website without search parameters, or the campaign tag of the link).
privacy.sec2ItemB: Writing content: the sections and texts you create, stored server-side.
privacy.sec2ItemC: Device token: stored server-side exclusively as a SHA256 hash.
privacy.sec2ItemD: Technical server logs: IP address, timestamp and user agent for operational security.
privacy.sec3Body: The data is used to provide the writing and synchronisation service (performance of contract) and for operational security and abuse prevention (legitimate interest).
privacy.sec4Body: The service is operated by the operator self-hosted on its own infrastructure in Switzerland; no external hosting provider is used. All account and writing content is stored on these servers in Switzerland.
privacy.secAiBody: For analysis, editing, book review and chat, the relevant writing content is transmitted to an AI service. Which service is used is configured per user account. By default, Anthropic's models (Claude) are used; the content is then transmitted to Anthropic in the USA for processing (transfer to a third country; for this, Anthropic relies on contractual safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses). Alternatively, a model self-hosted on the operator's infrastructure can be configured, in which case no content is transmitted to external third parties. The transmitted content is processed solely to provide the requested function and, under the provider's API terms, is not used to train its models.
privacy.sec5Body: No data is shared for advertising or analytics purposes. The service runs on the operator's own infrastructure; no external data processors are used for hosting. The spell checker (LanguageTool) and the dictation feature (speech-to-text) also run self-hosted; no content is transmitted to external third parties in the process. The only transmission of content to an external service concerns AI processing and is described separately in the section "AI Processing of Content".
privacy.sec6Body: In the native macOS client, content is first stored locally on your device and only synchronised with the server you selected. The device token used for sign-in is held exclusively in the macOS Keychain and does not leave your device in plain text.
privacy.sec7Body: You have the right to access, rectification, erasure, data portability and objection. You can request deletion of your account and data at any time by informal email to bede.berger@gmail.com. You have the right to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority (Switzerland: FDPIC; EU: the respective competent data protection authority).
privacy.sec8Body: Only technically necessary session cookies are set. No tracking or profiling takes place.
privacy.sec8BodyAnalytics: Only technically necessary session cookies are set. No profiling takes place. For anonymous, cookieless audience measurement, see the section “Audience measurement”.
privacy.secAnalyticsBody: For anonymous audience measurement we use Plausible Analytics, self-hosted on the operator's infrastructure. Plausible uses no cookies and stores no personal data; it records only aggregated metrics such as page views, referrers and coarse device and origin information, none of which allow individuals to be identified or tracked across multiple websites. The purpose is the statistical analysis of usage to improve the service; the legal basis is the legitimate interest in secure and user-friendly operation. No data is shared with third parties. In addition, we record technical attributes without any personal reference (the surface being used, language, display mode, type of work, your own role in the book, class of the model in use); book, section and user identifiers are not transmitted but stripped from the address before sending. Measurement also covers the public reading views of shared links; a share link's token is likewise stripped and never transmitted.
privacy.sec9Body: This privacy policy may be amended. The version published on this page at any given time is authoritative.

wortschatz.title: Vocabulary
wortschatz.intro: Length-robust measures across the whole book: how broad the vocabulary is, which words you use conspicuously often, and which phrases run through the manuscript. Measured on word forms rather than lemmas — “geht” and “ging” therefore count as two.

wortschatz.kpi.typesNote: Number of distinct word forms. It necessarily grows with book length, so it is useless for comparison — that is what MATTR and MTLD next to it are for.
wortschatz.kpi.mattrShort: Text shorter than the measuring window (only {window} words) — this value is the plain type-token ratio and is not comparable across books.
wortschatz.kpi.yuleNote: Concentration on few words. Lower is richer — the only measure here where small is better.
wortschatz.kpi.heapsNote: Vocabulary growth across the book. Around 0.5 is normal; near 0 means that past some point almost only familiar words appear.
wortschatz.kpi.mattrNote: Share of distinct words in a 1,000-word window that slides through the book one word at a time, then averaged. Because the window is always the same size, book length does not matter. Higher is more varied; 0.70 means that on average 700 of 1,000 words are distinct.
wortschatz.kpi.mtldNote: How many words in a row pass on average before repetition pushes the share of distinct words below 72%. Measured forwards and backwards, then averaged. Higher is more varied.
wortschatz.kpi.densityNote: Share of content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, proper names) among all words; the rest are function words such as articles, pronouns, prepositions. High reads dense and factual, lower narrative and spoken — neither is better.
wortschatz.kpi.hapaxNote: How many of the distinct words occur exactly once in the whole book.
wortschatz.kpi.source.mtld: Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity — McCarthy & Jarvis (2010)
wortschatz.kpi.source.heaps: Heaps' law V = K·N^β — Herdan (1960), Heaps (1978)

admin.settings.label.jobsBookChatMaxInpu: Book chat (agent): max input tokens per answer
admin.settings.label.jobsPageChatPreRagT: Section chat: book context top-K (0 = off)
admin.settings.help.komplettEffortExtrac: Claude only, full analysis only: effort level for exactly the call group that also uses the extraction model (full extraction, completeness gaps, coverage audit/feedback, scene backfill, life events). Empty = follows the full-analysis effort. Why: extraction is enumeration, not judgement — the thinking depth of the continuity check is wasted there, and because reasoning tokens bill against the same output budget as the JSON, this is the most direct cost and duration lever. Recommended: medium here, high/xhigh above. If recall drops (coverage score falls, fewer figures/locations), raise it again. The value feeds the cache version — changing it discards the extraction caches.
admin.settings.help.jobsBookChatMaxToolI: Separate, lower cap for local models; only takes effect when below the general value. 0 = no separate cap. Without prompt caching every iteration pays the full prompt again.
admin.settings.help.jobsBookChatMaxInput: Cost cap: cumulative input tokens across all tool rounds of one answer (cache included). Once reached, the chat answers from what it has gathered instead of researching further. 0 = off.
admin.settings.help.jobsBookChatToolSet: Auto: full catalogue for cloud/frontier models, curated subset (16 tools) for local ones. The full catalogue costs about 10,000 input tokens per iteration, which an endpoint without prompt caching pays again every round — and smaller models pick more reliably from 16 tools than from 37.
admin.settings.help.jobsResearchChatMaxW: Total cap across all rounds of one answer. Each Anthropic web search costs on top of tokens; once the cap is reached, the chat no longer offers the tool.
admin.settings.help.toolsOpenaiCompat: On (default): the agentic book chat may offer tools to this endpoint (OpenAI function calling). Off: the book chat runs classic (sections loaded up front). Turn off when endpoint or model do not speak a tool protocol — if the endpoint rejects a tool call, the job falls back to the classic path on its own anyway.
admin.settings.help.bookchatModelOpenaiC: Model for the book chat only. Empty = follows the default model above. Useful when the same endpoint serves several models and the chat should use a different one than proofreading and analysis — for the agentic path what matters most is how reliably the model calls tools.
admin.settings.help.bookchatContextWindo: Context window for the book chat only. 0 = follows the value above. Set it to what the chat model actually supports — the tool loop's input budget is derived from it.
admin.settings.help.bookchatMaxTokensOut: Output cap for the book chat only. 0 = follows the value above. The most effective lever for the agentic path: output cap and input budget share the same context window, and a chat answer rarely needs more than a few thousand tokens.
admin.settings.help.bookchatTimeoutMsOpe: Hard timeout per call for the book chat only. 0 = follows the value above.

Minimum similarity for core passages (score floor)

Cosine floor (0–1) for the passages of a psychological core in the text. Deliberately higher than the general embedding floor: a core is a meaning, not a string — weak hits there are systematically noise, and they would produce an arc band that glows everywhere and therefore says nothing. Applied at anchoring time, because the index feeds the arc measurement. 0 = off.

profile.aiAccess.title: Own AI access
profile.aiAccess.intro: Add your own API access – Claude (Anthropic) or an OpenAI-compatible provider. While it is set, all your AI features run through it, at your own cost. The key is stored encrypted and never shown again.
profile.aiAccess.hostHint: Provider base URL without /v1, e.g. https://api.openai.com. Publicly reachable addresses only.
profile.aiAccess.modelHintClaude: Empty = the Claude model this instance uses.
profile.aiAccess.modelHintOpenai: Model ID as the provider expects it.
profile.aiAccess.keyHint: Stored encrypted and only used for calls to this provider.
profile.aiAccess.cloudHint: On: full prompts and parallel calls, as with Claude (e.g. GPT-4.1). Off: slim prompts for small models.
profile.aiAccess.windowHint: Leave empty if you don't know your model's limits.
